# Live Performance — operator runbook

## First-night worker logs

These are worker diagnostics, not listener counts or proof of audible playback.
Identical codes (and HTTP statuses) log immediately on first occurrence, then
summarize repeats every 60 seconds; recovery flushes pending counts first.
Client closes are aggregated separately and are not gateway failures. The
30-second gateway timeout covers response headers, not the full audio download.

| Log | Meaning and operator action |
| --- | --- |
| `MEDIA_CLIENT_CLOSED` | Listener ended a download early; normal by itself. Investigate only alongside playback complaints. |
| `MEDIA_GATEWAY_HTTP status=…` | Gateway rejected a media request; inspect provider status and limits. |
| `MEDIA_GATEWAY_ERROR` | Gateway fetch or stream failed; check connectivity and provider health. |
| `MEDIA_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT` | Gateway did not return headers in time; check provider latency. |
| `MEDIA_GATEWAY_RECOVERED` | A later media response completed after a gateway failure; keep monitoring. |
| `ROOM_STATE_UNAVAILABLE` | Live room state or receiver tick failed; inspect hosting and durable storage. |
| `ROOM_STATE_RECOVERED` | A later room tick succeeded; independently verify the live return. |
| `[rpc] Alchemy budget mode …` | Budget mode changed; inspect the GET `/health` RPC budget summary before operator action. |

`HEAD /health` is a bodyless uptime check; GET `/health` supplies the existing
provider and RPC summary. Deployment and real-staging verification are separate
from local tests.

## Production desk: live-session coordination

The Admin booking card's **Open production desk** link opens
`producer-room.html?booking=…`. Its roster is the public booking schedule, **not**
a private access grant. Select a booking and sign with the existing configured
owner wallet. Each selected room needs its own pass; unexpired passes stay only
in that tab's memory and clear on wallet change, expiry or page exit. No new
engineer/staff role is enabled.

The desk separates the canonical public radio act from the selected private
room. It never automatically plays public radio or opens the operator microphone.
Selecting/listening never changes the program; only explicit server-enabled
allocated-stage commands can do so. **Listen to selected room** disconnects the old private subscription
before opening the next. Mute public radio in other tabs/devices; use headphones.
Use **Open full soundcheck room** for the existing actual check/arm workflow.
Private practice remains separately authorized in its existing rehearsal room.

If an unfired asset booking was closed before its booked start because booking
verification was unavailable, check that it is still accepted, funded, and not
cancelled. Reconnect the configured owner to the full soundcheck room. Only
sign a recovery message that explicitly says it reopens the booking for
private soundchecks. Have the performer reconnect and run both checks again
within their official windows. This does not reopen ended or allocated sets,
change escrow, or take the room on air.

Owner and performer share one booking-private text thread using their existing
backstage passes. The owner can cue **another song** or **wrap up after this
song**, and notify the next performer of a possible delay or standby. The

performer can acknowledge a cue, report ready/not ready, notify the owner that
they are not playing, and declare their set
finished. Acknowledgment is not musical completion, schedule-change consent,
payment approval or an instruction to cut the feed. Standby acknowledgment is
optional and does not gate owner notifications. **Not playing this slot** first
marks the performer not ready, then sends a private notice; neither action
cancels the booking or waives the original guaranteed fee. If either save fails,
the panel shows the failure rather than claiming both succeeded.

Messages, cues, readiness and presence are memory-only, bounded live-session
state. The panel displays server-reported retention and expiry. A worker restart,
booking end/cancellation or session expiry clears access/history; reconnect and
confirm readiness after a reset. There is no saved transcript or offline delivery.
Do not put secrets in the thread. Lost responses are not automatically resent:
**Retry same action** reuses the command ID in the same session epoch; after a
reset, review current state instead. Presence only reflects performer heartbeats,
not audio delivery. A stale direction service disables sending without stopping
the performer's microphone.

The **advisory direction card** never extends airtime, cuts the broadcast or takes
an act live. Use the separate allocated-stage controls below, only when the worker
returns their capabilities. [#343](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking/issues/343)
still needs the integrated two-act/device rehearsal and release verification;
an “another song” cue alone is never permission to play past the authorized end.
Original contract times and guaranteed fees remain unchanged.

### Anonymous listener feedback and verified tip notices (#341)

With the matching site and worker versions, a guest can send applause, love,
encore or **Can't hear** from the radio footer during the currently verified,
armed live set. No wallet, sign-in or free-text message is required. Controls
disable when the live state is stale or unavailable, and disappear in archive
mode or after the effective set ends. Signals are advisory: an encore request
never extends airtime, and a report never cancels a show or changes payment.

The performer room and the owner-authorized production desk show anonymous
counts for the last 30 seconds and two minutes, plus browser counts and an
audio-problem warning. A browser is not a verified person; refreshes, shared
networks, dropped requests and limits can affect the count. An empty report is
**not proof that listeners can hear**: independently listen to the public
return. If the private pass, booking verification or feedback service goes
stale, the panel says so and does not change microphone, monitoring or
broadcast controls. The performer can turn off the small floating reactions
and tip notices beside the publish controls; the detailed panel follows the
audio controls. The visual strip cannot intercept input, and reduced-motion
settings show static notices. The owner desk receives counts without a public
overlay. Longer amounts that cannot fit in the compact notice are replaced
with “Tip received”; the detailed panel shows the exact latest confirmed tip
and verified set total.

Tip notices and the set's ETH total come from the separate native-tip ledger,
not the browser's payment assertion. Only successfully confirmed, canonical
Base router events with verified source, exact booking and performer recipient,

and a timestamp inside the effective live window qualify. Self-tips, pending,
reverted, mismatched and old direct transfers are not shown as verified.
The ledger may lag or be unavailable while indexing, rebuilding after a reorg,
or verifying a source; **so far** means the total may be incomplete. A room's
first snapshot establishes a baseline rather than replaying older notices;
only up to 20 recent tip entries are used for notifications. These are brief
“tip received” notices, not listener-authored notes. Existing tip routing and
the guaranteed performer fee are unchanged.

Signals and their per-browser/network rate-limit identifiers are held only in
worker memory, with no identity opt-in, durable transcript, IPFS checkpoint or
Discord publication. The display has no wallet or network addresses. Recent
events expire after 10 seconds, counts cover at most two minutes, and idle
hashed browser records expire after 130 seconds with a cleanup sweep at most
10 seconds later. The latest anonymous signal time remains for the current set.
All set-specific feedback is cleared when that set ends, changes, is cancelled
or the worker restarts; rate-limit records may remain briefly to enforce limits.
Defaults are two seconds between signals and 12 per browser/minute, 60 per
network/minute and 600 globally/minute. Shared networks and IPv6 /64 grouping
can limit several listeners together.

Before any release, confirm the actual trusted reverse-proxy topology and set
`LIVE_FEEDBACK_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` accordingly; see the
[worker configuration](../discord-bot/README.md#anonymous-live-audience-feedback).
Never merge or deploy during a live show without the separate owner approval and
safe handoff. Local tests and a mocked browser are not a real performer or

live-tip test. Keep #341 open until a guest and authorized performer/operator
exercise the flow in a real show, including a real verified tip and public-audio
check.

### Public listener telemetry and rehearsal evidence (#362 / #348)

With matching site and worker code, select the **currently public** live booking
and use its existing owner pass on the production desk. The telemetry panel
reports observed active page connections, peak, reconnects in up to the last
hour, and approximate time-to-first-audio histogram percentiles. Use **Export
aggregate evidence** while the show is still live and the snapshot is fresh;
the JSON contains aggregates only. There is no post-show retrieval: save the
export before the public set ends. Another selected booking, stale verification,
expired authorization, malformed responses, and network/service errors show
unavailable, not a healthy zero. The observation start in the export is when
this worker first observed the show, not necessarily its beginning. A worker
restart resets the measurements. The last aggregate stays in memory until a
different show is observed or the worker stops; it is not checkpointed.

Counts are an estimate of participating pages, not unique people, actual
capacity, or a full census. A tab with several tracked audio sources shares one
lease; separate tabs/reloads do not. The browser sends connect only after its
public room connects, and first audio only when playback is unpaused and
unmuted with nonzero element volume and inbound audio packets advance. Duration
starts before obtaining the listener grant, ends at the first qualifying stats
check (normally one-second resolution), and is omitted after 120 seconds.
The p50/p95 are upper bounds of fixed histogram buckets, not exact durations.
Packets and element playback cannot establish that sound reached speakers or a
person heard it; silent input, OS mute and device routing are not detected.

Reconnects count completed page-level reconnections, not failed attempts.
The last-hour number sums 60 one-minute buckets, omitting the oldest partial
minute; reason totals are since observation start. Empty samples have unavailable
percentiles. Independently monitor the public return.

The page creates a random ID in memory only, and obtains an opaque telemetry
token only alongside an admitted public listener grant. Neither is linked to a
wallet, account or profile. Accepted event sequence and lease state, including
the random page ID, token, last sequence, connection/first-audio flags, last
activity time and short-lived leave tombstones, remain only in worker memory for
45 seconds after issuance or the last accepted event/renewal, swept on a
five-second timer subject to scheduler delays; at most 2,000 such records exist.
They are not an event history. Heartbeats normally
run every 15 seconds. After admission the page also holds a signed renewal
capability in memory, bound to that random page ID and public-show lifecycle,
valid until the earlier of the show end or four hours. The worker verifies it
with a process-random secret without keeping a separate capability record.
Renewal rotates the capability and can restore an expired observation without
requesting another LiveKit seat or incrementing connects. On pagehide the page
sends leave and clears its lease token; a restored page can renew if its source
is still connected. The capability and source state remain in that page's
memory only, not browser storage. A long-running active page renews near expiry;
an expired capability, changed show or worker restart cannot be renewed, so
observation remains unavailable until a new public listener grant; browser

clock skew can also stop renewal early. No automatic extra room seat is opened.
If a first
connection arrives after its original lease expires, it can be observed through
renewal but is conservatively omitted from the connect total.

A missed leave, suspended tab or failed network request can under- or over-count
until expiry or successful renewal. Renewal and reconnect reports are
client-asserted: a bearer can renew after leaving, so renewal is not proof of
a current LiveKit seat. While an active page has a valid capability, automatic
background recovery retries one renewal operation every 30 seconds until the
capability expires, with up to two HTTP attempts per operation. An uncertain
failed reconnect is not replayed as a new event, so reconnect totals can
under-count. Network/rate errors may leave the page unmeasured. A rapid
replacement while the preceding leave is still pending can also be unmeasured
rather than delay audio. No local storage, raw event history, audio, chat, user
agent, wallet or IP is stored in telemetry records or exports. Unexpected
failures produce generic, rate-limited worker/browser warnings without request
identifiers or error details (at most one per minute per worker/browser module
under a normal clock); playback is independent of telemetry.

For rate limiting, the worker transiently normalizes the source network and
holds only its process-random HMAC key (IPv6 grouped by /64), last-charge time
and rolling hit times. Each hit expires from the rolling window after 60 seconds.
An idle key is removed 60 seconds after its **last charged request**, on a
subsequent request or the five-second cleanup sweep; scheduler delays can defer
the sweep. A continuously active network key can remain until activity stops,

the 2,000-key bound evicts it, or the worker stops, including across shows.
The salt and all keys are memory-only and reset at worker restart. Defaults are
300 events/network/minute and 6,000 globally/minute; rate limits and admission
can drop real reports. The same
trusted proxy configuration as feedback must match the actual deployment.
Native HTTP, hosting and providers may still see source IPs in access logs;
this feature does not configure or control those logs.

Tokens and origin checks deter arbitrary event submission but do not prove
unique humans, real hearing or prevent a client that can obtain public grants
from inflating counts. Private rehearsals and soundchecks do not issue these
public telemetry grants. Metrics do not affect attendance, credit, recording,
payments or broadcast policy. Local simulated clients are not the #348 staging
ramp or evidence of any listener capacity; complete the separately approved
real rehearsal and predeployment checks before relying on these measurements.

### Explicit allocated-stage controls

1. Authorize the current booking with the existing owner wallet, then **Enable
   allocated-stage control**. This can adopt a currently live contracted set.
   Unallocated bookings retain their legacy automatic scheduling.
2. In the desk, select the exact next act and **Reserve and notify selected next
   act**. The owner must separately authorize that next booking; the current
   room's pass cannot grant access to it. This slice coordinates the current and
   selected next act only, not an all-night schedule or third-booking cascade.
   Bump notices do not require the artist's acknowledgment or consent, but the
   delayed artist chooses **decline**, a positive short duration no longer than
   the contract, or the full contracted length from the actual delayed start.
   All choices retain the original guarantee.
3. Real checks use the effective planned start; existing passed checks remain
   real checks, not retroactive credit. Both checks, fresh delivered audio,
   performer choice/readiness and the owner's explicit take are required.
   Arming an allocated stage confirms readiness; it is not an automatic take.
4. **Authorize additional encore** records extra minutes, capped cumulatively
   at ten per allocated set. If a next act is paired, its separate owner pass is
   required again before a bump. Read the server-confirmed effective times; the
   immutable original start/end and financial terms are shown separately.
5. The performer's **My allocated set is finished** is the durable declaration
   required for a normal producer ending. An advisory finished note is not a
   substitute. **Force cut** is explicitly interrupted, never a successful
   curtain call. The owner may **Take this selected act live** only after the

predecessor has ended and the backend verifies checks, timing, choice,
   readiness, audio and protected-paid-program boundaries.
6. Existing passes retain their original expiration. Use **Refresh allocated
   booking pass · keep microphone on** for the new bounded access window;
   this does not stop or republish the microphone. Stale/failed commands disable
   controls and never claim success. An uncertain durable result can be retried
   with the same command ID rather than submitting another extension.
   After the original end, Profile checks pending/unknown allocations against a
   fresh exact-booking public audio snapshot before offering **Return to allocated
   backstage**. This also works when the original fee is already approved/paid.
   The link does not grant access or prove public playback; authorize the booked
   wallet in the room, and do not open a second publishing microphone. A failed,
   stale, expired or mismatched lookup offers a status refresh instead of claiming
   the set finished. Original contract times, receipts and claim rights stay separate.
7. Admin's actual-stage completion is separate from fee approval/claim. A
   pending or unknown allocated completion blocks new review/release workflows,
   not truthful reconciliation of an already-submitted transaction. The
   original guarantee, on-chain review window and claim deadline remain
   unchanged. A priority invitation flag is follow-up only—not an automatically
   accepted, funded or scheduled booking.
8. **Quiet endings (#343).** Ask the performer to keep the microphone on until the
   producer ends the set. If a set the performer declared finished goes quiet and
   nobody ends it, the server closes it after the audio grace (15 seconds under

the **#358 policy**, previously about a minute) as the normal
   producer-finished ending, timed at the later of the declaration and the last
   audio. That is never an audio-loss cancellation, so no fault slate or
   recovery-ads window runs. With legacy recording segments, if the producer's
   **End** lands more than five seconds after the audio stopped, the recording is
   flagged incomplete and its radio title gains "(partial recording)", because
   the recorder compares captured
   seconds with the set's actual window. With frame-timed segments enabled (see
   rollout below), capture is compared with the first-to-last audio window:
   a quiet 30-second wait for **End** alone does not make the recording partial.
   Actual capture gaps, capture failures and abnormal endings still do.
   An approved encore withdraws the finished declaration, so a silent room is
   again treated as an audio fault. Evidence:
   `node --test test/night-simulation.test.js` replays a two-act night on a fake
   clock; it is a simulation of this server's state machine, not a live-audio test.

### Producer recovery (#358)

The owner authorized **15 seconds** for an unfinished set to recover and at most
**one additional minute cumulative per set**, explicitly granted by the producer.
This supersedes the older Friday 60-second default. Read the server countdown
and remaining budget in the stage controls; a reconnect/reload/restart never
replenishes it. **Grant explicit recovery hold** is separate from encore and
cannot extend the set's existing authorized end or change guaranteed pay.

Use **Run commercials now** or **Run radio now** rather than waiting in silence.
These preserve the set until its current deadline; they are not cancellation
and add no recovery time. The performer can reconnect privately. Only
**Return recovered performer safely**, after real audio and fresh performer
readiness, returns from filler at a safe paid-song/advert boundary. At expiry,
the existing terminal cancellation/fault/advert/radio path runs once. A finished
declaration still follows #343's normal ending; terminal cancellation cannot
be undone.

For the next act, open their booking from the roster or **Open paired next
act**, authorize that exact owner scope, and use the existing private message,
standby and readiness panel. Opening is not a sent message. No-next-act,
not-ready, unavailable/denied and expired/stale status must stay honest.
**Advance paired ready next act** explicitly ends the interrupted original set
and takes the ready paired performer atomically, even before the original start,
only with their actual fresh readiness, chosen participation, genuine checks,
fresh audio, funding/authorization, protected schedules and safe paid boundary.
It is never automatic; normal **Take** retains its original-start safeguard.

Filler is not the artist's performance or completion evidence. Capture gaps
remain interrupted/partial. Existing recording permissions are not expanded:
early-taken audio before the original contracted start is excluded and any
resulting recording is partial. Consent, release approval, pay and escrow/claim
rules remain unchanged.

Release requires the [reader-first and mirror checks](LIVE_AUDIO_PILOT.md#producer-recovery-358):
first deploy compatible readers with `LIVE_AUDIO_RECOVERY_ENABLED` unset/false
and explicitly retain `LIVE_AUDIO_GRACE_MS=60000`. The default is 15000 even with
recovery writes disabled, so omitting the override changes the watchdog before
producer controls exist. This temporary override is only for reader-only rollout.
Later, after reader/restore verification, compatible controls and separate
approval, activate both settings together: `LIVE_AUDIO_GRACE_MS=15000` and
`LIVE_AUDIO_RECOVERY_ENABLED=true`. Initial unarmed automatic slots retain their
separate 60-second allowance regardless of the lost-audio grace setting.
Old decrypted readers reject the optional recovery
field; the current local mirror client already rejects encrypted live lifecycle
envelopes, so retain approved hosted-verified storage or approve a separate
mirror reader upgrade. Never erase the hold journal or bypass
`node radio-predeploy.js`. Real staging
audio/OBS/reconnect/messages/paid-boundary/recording checks are **NOT RUN**.

Backstage/monitoring/consent/fee regressions (the original 102-test selection,
now including Profile re-entry cases):

```bash

node --test test/{live-broadcast-controls,live-direction-ui,private-room-listener,producer-room,performer-room,input-monitor,live-publisher-presence,live-audio-wiring,live-recording-option,live-recording-room,live-recording-consent,live-escrow-release}.test.js
```

The reproducible **Profile-only** browser harness is
`test/browser/live-profile-reentry.html`. Serve the repository locally and use
**Run browser checks** at 390px and 1280px. Its nine mocked cases cover waiting,
live, approved/paid, stale/offline/expired/mismatched state and forced ending;
it neither connects a wallet nor publishes audio or proves a real live show.
Earlier inline room/producer browser checks did not persist a reusable harness.

New recording opt-ins explicitly sign **permission v2** for this booking's
authorized on-air set, including an authorized delayed start, the artist's chosen
short/full set and at most ten minutes of producer-approved encore. This
permission neither grants extra airtime nor changes the original fee/terms.
Private practice and soundchecks remain excluded. Existing checked v1 permission
still covers **only the original scheduled set**. Its visible **Update recording
permission for delay / encore** action requires a fresh performer signature and
an explicit v2 server confirmation. Declined, unavailable or legacy-only responses
never widen the previous permission. Published IPFS audio cannot be recalled.

After going off air, the performer can open the Studio from the room.
Profile also offers the right-side Studio for ended asset and pilot bookings.
Preview unlocks after processing. An unfinished edit saved in the current
browser shows a resume reminder in Profile. Saving a draft or leaving it
unfinished cannot approve release, mint, or change performance pay. An artist

may approve the full set, approve named cuts, or publish nothing. Admin mint
review is separate. Verified recordings over ten minutes are eligible only in

## Attributed native ETH tips (#355; release gate)

The feature branch routes live, radio-recording and archive-recording tips through
the dedicated DecentBusking tip contract **only when configured**. It forwards
100% of the tip to the selected artist; wallet gas is additional. This is not the
USDC payroll router, a supporter gift, custody, or a new fee. Until enabled, the
hat explicitly labels the existing direct-transfer route as having no on-chain
DecentBusking attribution. A broken configured route never falls back to it.

The `TipSent` event binds sender, recipient, exact native wei, source kind and
context. Canonical references are `decentbusking:live:<bookingId>` and
`decentbusking:radio:<chain>:<collection>:<tokenId>` (or `archive` instead of
`radio`). Source kinds are 0/1/2 respectively. The contract route proves use of
the protocol, **not which browser page was open or that a performance happened**.
Caller labels alone never establish verified artist/source earnings.

The separate `/api/tips/ledger?wallet=<address>&offset=0&limit=25` read API verifies
successful receipts, two Base confirmations, canonical blocks and exact events.
Event identity includes chain, contract, transaction and log index; repeated tips
are not deduplicated by show or recording. Live recipients are checked against
`bookings(keccak256(bookingId))` at the receipt block. Recording identity, existence
and tip wallet are checked using the allowlisted NFT's URI/metadata at that block,
not today's owner or a caller-selected wallet. Unavailable or mismatched source
proof stays explicitly unverified, separate from attributed totals. Self-transfers
are not counted as earnings. The Profile's collapsed **Native ETH tips** section

shows precise ETH amounts and transaction/log proofs without changing USDC totals.

### Cancellation / incident procedure

- **Cancel live performance** requires a public reason and explicit confirmation, then signs an owner command. It invokes the existing #227 dated-occurrence cancellation mechanism; the public cancellation retains artist/title, original time and reason. Normal radio continues; future Fridays remain. Verify public schedule and admin schedule **synced**. Refresh/reopen clients; existing calendar polling receives the shared schedule update.
- Financial consequences are **separate**. Panel displays the agreed proposed kill-fee amount and pending financial reconciliation. Phase 0 has no automatic contract kill fee or refund; **Reconcile financial cancellation** records a report/reason/disposition and the agreed fee, then **Execute recorded payment decision** and **Recover agreed remainder** each require a separate explicit owner transaction. Review agreed terms and actual deposits before authorizing either. No refund is fabricated.
- If a checkpoint fails, cancellation intent remains durable with **schedule failed**; retry linkage with **Link / retry schedule occurrence**, then verify public calendar/radio. Do not claim cancellation succeeded while schedule sync failed. During a slot, schedule cancellation works; Phase 1 pre-show cancel does not, so review/reject after end is required.
- Wrong network/account: signing is blocked. On a wallet/network change or failed signature, refresh and reconcile the original hash. Transactions that were submitted can still mine after UI errors. Local pending hashes survive reload; backend revisions and unique occurrence/booking/tx IDs prevent duplicate records; router completed work references prevent double payout.
- Worker restore errors disable mutations instead of seeding over unknown state. Never erase checkpoints or manually edit production state to “fix” a pending transaction.

# Your First Visit To DecentBusking

Start here: [open DecentBusking](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/). You can listen and explore without connecting a wallet. Take the listener route first; submit a song only when you are ready to share it publicly.

## Follow The White Rabbit

Look for **Follow the white rabbit** in the center of the landing scene. The large
**☿** Mercury symbol follows the rabbit with a small flying-money icon and
different musical accessories at every stop. Mercury is a visual companion,
not a narrator. A white rabbit peeks out of little rabbit holes beside each
stop, with factual text explaining the controls. The tour opens the actual
briefcase, Top 10, DVert, DJuke, archive, and both ankh menus, explaining what each
is for without voting, submitting, connecting a wallet, paying, or starting audio.

Choose **Follow**, **Back**, or **Leave tour** at your own pace. Arrow keys move
between stops when the card has focus; Tab also lets you explore the page. On exit,
previously open drawers and any visible briefcase draft are restored. Finish any
pending submission, close other dialogs, and return from VertLoop to main radio
before starting. Reduced-motion settings keep the rabbit and Mercury still.
The card count sits beside **Follow the White Rabbit**. A centered hole in the
card is the rabbit's home: it dives down, emerges beside the highlighted feature
with a short hop and sparkles, and returns home before the next card appears.
Navigation pauses briefly during the trip; **Leave tour** and **Close tutorial**
remain available. Outside clicks and Escape do not dismiss the tour.
Reduced motion skips the trip and decorative effects.
After completing every stop, the landing-page button is hidden in that browser.
Leaving early does not count as completion. Click **DBusker** to open **About**
and use the identical **Follow the white rabbit** button to replay the tour.
Music notes and little sound-wave rings accompany Mercury's arrivals. These are
visual effects, not extra audio over the radio.

### Build a DJuke playlist with the bunny

[Open the playlist tutorial](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/?tutorial=playlists).
This link opens directly to the playlist card even if you have already completed
the general tour. The same card is included after DJuke in the full walkthrough.
Mercury follows the bunny between the real controls:

1. Search for a song or creator and choose a song.
2. Use **Add selected song** to build a draft of up to 24 songs.
3. Name the mix, reorder with **↑ / ↓**, or remove a song with **×**.
4. **Save to Profile** signs and keeps a named revision, without buying playback.
5. **Personal Play** buys your mix at creator prices for your ears only.
6. **Play Live** queues it for the community, at the displayed radio tier prices
   plus $3 per started group of 12 songs. Base network gas is additional.
   Protected hours/shows can set your mix aside; remaining songs return to the
   queue afterward without another payment.
   There is no refund solely for that delay or interruption. Separate
   failed-delivery refunds still apply; exact playback times are not guaranteed.
   If your estimated playlist/current/queued playback overlaps a protected block
   on the public calendar, checkout names the show and asks before proceeding.
   Unknown song lengths use a rough four-minute-per-song allowance; ordinary
   checkout without a detected overlap has no separate confirmation window.
7. See how song payments split 90% to musicians/collaborators, 8% to pinning, and
   2% to development, while the separate radio fee splits 25% each to Playback,
   Top 10, Pinners, and Development. The radio fee settles after full delivery.
8. See a labeled illustration of your playlist taking the radio stage after the

current song and protected shows. Main paid requests can cut in between songs.

**Follow** and **Back** move through these hops without editing your draft,
signing, paying, or changing the live radio. Empty/unavailable controls stay
disabled. The fee-flow and radio illustrations are explanations, not payment
receipts or a live takeover. Ending this linked guide leaves DJuke open to try;
leaving early restores the original drawer and playlist disclosure state.

## Three Names, One Community

| Name | What you are looking at |
| --- | --- |
| **DecentBusking** | The website: live radio, the music NFT archive, artist tips, submissions, and playback tallies. |
| **#DecentJukebox** | The Discord channel where artists post songs and the bot handles upload and NFT-request replies. |
| **JukeLoop** | The ongoing community radio rotation in Discord voice, synchronized to the website's radio. |

An NFT is a token referring to a song and its metadata. Owning or minting the token does not, by itself, transfer copyright or grant music-use rights.

## 1. Listen First

![DecentBusking header, music space, and radio controls](../img/newcomer-listen.png)

Look at the **bottom radio bar**. It shows the current song and artist when JukeLoop is playing.

The screenshot shows the first-load view while the archive and radio are loading. Song artwork and the current track will change; a star field alone does not mean you need to connect a wallet.

1. Click **Tune in** if it appears. Browsers can require a click before sound starts.
2. Use the **speaker button** to mute or unmute, and the **volume control** beside it to adjust the radio.
3. If you see a between-tracks or reconnecting message, wait for the next track. Repeated clicks will not manufacture a live stream.

**You have reached this step when:** you can hear the current track and recognize its title and artist. No wallet or payment is required.

## 2. Vote On What Is Playing

Click **thumbs up** or **thumbs down** in the bottom radio bar while a track is active. Disabled voting buttons mean there is no eligible current play yet. The site accepts one vote per browser for that play, not a new vote for every click.

Votes influence the radio rotation. New Top 10 prize drafts use weekly net votes, but prizes need a funded budget and owner review. A vote is not a payment or a guarantee of earnings.

**You have reached this step when:** the vote control acknowledges your choice.

For a problem that needs steward attention, choose **Flag for review** on the
radio or NFT card. Select Inappropriate, Mislabeled, Copyright, or Other; Other
needs a short explanation. Connect your wallet and sign the report, without a
payment. A report requests review; it does not automatically ban a recording.
See [Content Review](CONTENT-REVIEW.md) for radio scopes and paid-request handling.

## 3. Meet A Song And Its Artist

Select a music NFT in the **3D music space / archive**. Inspect its song details and artwork. Click **Preview** for a free 30-second taste or **Listen** to play the whole song. Selecting an archive recording is different from listening to the live radio: use **Radio** in the bottom bar to return to JukeLoop.

Click **Archive** near the upper-right of the music space for the song list, or use **Search Artist or Song** below the header. Wait for metadata to load if the archive is initially empty.

The **hat** opens the tip form. A tip is a real wallet payment, not a free interaction. Check the destination, token, amount, network, and wallet fees before confirming. You do not need to send a tip to keep exploring.

The **Left Ankh** at the top opens the public **Playback Tally**. This is the whole station's activity, not just your songs. Admin and Payroll entries are owner tools; ordinary listeners do not need them.

**You have reached this step when:** you can tell the difference between an archive song, the live radio, and the public tally.

## 4. Bring One Song

![The Submit Your Busk form and its information button](../img/newcomer-submit.png)

Choose one route. Do not submit the same song twice just because owner review takes time.

### Website Route

1. Click the **briefcase** to open **Bring your sound**.
2. Click the little **i** beside the heading and read **Your Music & Public Uploads** before choosing a file.
3. Connect your artist wallet using the **wallet control at the top-right**, then return to the briefcase. Artist actions use Base.
4. Enter the **Title** and **Artist / creator**. Drop supported audio or MP4 up to 50 MB, or choose **Already on IPFS** for an already-pinned file. A CID is not a folder path or a gateway URL; media format is detected automatically.
5. Artwork is optional and accepts an image file or IPFS CID independently of the media source. Check the artist wallet: that is where the approved NFT will go. Collaborator percentages apply only to DJuke creator earnings, not joint NFT ownership, royalties, weekly prizes, or tips. The alternate tip wallet is under the extra options. Referencing another token does not grant permission to use someone else's song. Mark DVert submissions as adverts; airtime is booked separately through DVert.
6. Click **Submit for Approval**. Wallet signatures authorize the upload/submission; read each prompt. This is not the owner's mint transaction.
7. Look for **Queued for owner approval** and the IPFS CID. Keep the CID and wait for review rather than repeatedly submitting.

**You have reached this step when:** the form says the song is queued. The artist request does not mint automatically, promise radio scheduling, or guarantee a payout. The owner reviews and pays gas for an approved mint sent to the chosen artist wallet.

The NFT's royalty setting describes a royalty request to compatible marketplaces, not guaranteed income or copyright ownership.

### Discord Route

1. [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa) and open **#DecentJukebox**.
2. Post one supported audio or MP4 attachment, up to 10 MB for this bot's attachment flow.
3. Read the bot reply and click **Request NFT** when offered. Enter your Base artist wallet and optional artwork as prompted.
4. Wait for owner review and the mint confirmation reply. Discord upload/playback and an NFT request are distinct steps; ask the admins before posting if you do not want your song played on radio.

To hear the Discord radio, join the **JukeLoop voice channel**. If an attachment is too large, use the website's upload or existing-file-CID route instead.

## Public Uploads: Know The Limits

![The upload rights and public storage notice](../img/newcomer-policy.png)

IPFS files can be downloaded, copied, and pinned by others. The information notice grants no AI-training permission, but cannot stop third-party scraping or guarantee that all public copies can be removed. The current form has no separate radio-consent or opt-out checkbox. If you do not want radio playback, contact the admins before submitting.

You can request that we stop future playlist playback or unpin our copy; that does not guarantee erasing other people's copies or immutable NFT records. This notice is information, not a signed licence or consent agreement. Share only material you have the right to share.

## 5. Find Your Own Songs And Counts

1. Connect the **same artist wallet used to receive your music NFT**.
2. Click the **Right Ankh** at the top-right of the title.
3. Choose **My Playbacks**. This opens **My Playback Tally**, filtered to the connected artist wallet.
4. Start with **All Time**, then choose a UTC week to inspect qualified weekly plays. Use song, artist, and upload-date filters to narrow the list.

The song rows show **Plays**, **Likes**, and **Dislikes**. Those like/dislike columns are lifetime totals even when you select a week. Playback payroll uses qualified weekly plays; Top 10 prize calculations separately use new weekly net-vote buckets. Weekly buckets start fresh on Monday UTC while lifetime totals remain.

**You have reached this step when:** you can find your own song and distinguish its lifetime activity from the selected week's qualified plays. If the list is empty, check the wallet, the date/search filters, and **All Time** first. Counts are not a withdrawable balance; owner-reviewed payments need a funded budget.

## 6. Keep A Copy And Share The Pinner Fund (Optional)

Musicians and listeners can keep a copy of our public music on their own computer with IPFS Desktop. Admin-approved nodes that pass independent hourly checks share the weekly pinner fund in Base USDC. Start with the [Earn by pinning guide](../wiki/Earn-by-Pinning.md), then open the header **IPFS** button.

## When Something Does Not Match

If you cannot hear the radio, check **Tune in**, mute, volume, and whether a track is actually live. If an upload is queued, wait for the owner rather than re-uploading. If a song or NFT is missing, keep the CID, artist wallet, and any confirmation transaction link, then [ask the admins on Discord](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa). Never send anyone your seed phrase or private key.

You now know the loop: **artist shares a song -> owner reviews an NFT request -> approved music appears in the archive and may join radio -> listeners hear and vote -> tallies record activity -> funded, reviewed payouts are a separate step.**
# DecentBusking Payroll

## Base Payroll Panel

Promotional offers use the separate **Promotionals (`dbusk-promotionals`)**
allocation, not artist or development payroll. Create/deposit using Left ankh →
Admin Community Calendar → Fund Allocations, then review offers and reward claims in Admin → Invites & Promotions.
See [promotions setup, activity rules and payment recovery](PROMOTIONS.md).

Active payroll is Base-only. Historical records are preserved outside the active queue; see [retired payroll history](LEGACY-PAYROLL.md). The public Left Ankh entry is Playback Tally; Admin Nft Mint and Payroll are visible only to the configured admin wallet. UI visibility does not replace transaction-level owner and role checks.

The panel opens with a week-first **Weekly Artist Payments** workspace: choose a completed week, review and back up receipts, then confirm wallet payments. Separate Playback and Top 10 cards show the unpaid amount, payment progress, readiness and the next required action. Missing receipts say **Not prepared**, not zero dollars. Expand a card's recipients to review wallets or copy technical payment references. There is no manual contributor-identity entry. Existing payment references and frozen amounts are unchanged.

**Estimates & allocation settings**, **Treasury & preparation details**, backup import, and Payment History & Proofs are collapsed secondary controls below the primary workflow. Router deposits and owner recovery now live in **Admin Community Calendar → Fund Allocations**, not Payroll. Repo Dev Bot Payouts remain separate; beneath them, **🎖 Supporter tokens owed** lists referral-campaign Supporter tokens to send directly from the admin wallet (see [Supporter tokens owed](PROMOTIONS.md#-supporter-tokens-owed)). New York budgets are automatically prepared from unreserved funds; legacy UTC receipts retain their existing amounts. Opening or previewing the panel never moves funds. Current-week shares are provisional; only closed weeks with published receipts can offer owner-authorized payouts.

Playback drafts group qualified weekly plays by verified artist wallet and distribute the selected budget proportionally with exact six-decimal token-unit rounding. The share calculation includes every qualified play, including plays whose artist has no valid wallet by the Monday New York cutoff. That artist's share is forfeited for the week, is not redistributed, and remains unreserved in the fund for the next week's budget. Amounts below the selected minimum and rounding remainder likewise stay unallocated. Current weeks remain provisional.

New Top 10 allocations rank individual songs by positive weekly net votes (upvotes minus downvotes), breaking ties by plays, title, then track ID, exactly like the public chart. First place receives half the unreserved weekly prize budget; each following place receives half the remainder, with the final ranked prize receiving the remaining amount when the minimum threshold requires consolidation. Prizes must exceed $0.10, so smaller pots fund fewer than ten places; pots of $0.10 or less remain unallocated. One artist may earn multiple song prizes. Each winning song has a separate payout reference. A winning song without a valid linked artist wallet by the Monday New York cutoff forfeits its assigned prize; that prize is not redistributed and remains unreserved in the Top 10 fund for the next week's budget. Current estimates refresh with votes and confirmed sponsor/advertising funding; closed-week receipts freeze at Monday midnight in America/New_York. Schema v5 records song IDs and titles; older artist-based receipts retain their existing amounts and paid-reference identities. Public site votes are anonymous and are not Sybil-resistant: these are owner-reviewed prizes, not a proof of unique humans. Playback payroll remains artist-based and uses qualified plays, not votes.

New payout plays and vote changes use `NY-YYYY-MM-DD` buckets starting Monday 00:00 `America/New_York`, including daylight-saving transitions. UTC history is also retained. The first New York week is partial from rollout; old aggregates are not relabelled. Old buckets and all-time counters survive rollover and restart. Repeated Discord count snapshots apply only their delta; historical backfill never creates new weekly prize votes.

Read-only treasury status checks USDC approval, fund existence/activity and balances, plus the owner's Base ETH gas balance. Separate fund slugs are `dbusk-playback` and `dbusk-top10`; the development fund is not used as the radio budget. Funds are never automatically created or funded.

### Admin Fund Allocations

Open **Left ankh → Admin Community Calendar → Fund Allocations** near the bottom
of the calendar. Its switchable bar/pie chart uses verified project allocations,
with separate ETH and USDC views. Opening this workspace does not fetch the
payroll queue or payment ledger. The chart shows total balances, not spendable
campaign budgets; incomplete registry metadata is reported, not invented.

For the first referral campaign:

1. Choose **Prepare referral fund**. The permanent slug is `dbusk-referrals`
   (plural). If already registered it selects that allocation instead.
2. Review the suggested name/purpose, save the public metadata to IPFS, then
   separately review and create the empty allocation on Base.
3. Enter the ETH amount and choose **Review ETH deposit**. Keep extra Base ETH
   for gas. Native funding needs no ERC-20 approval.
4. In the existing referral campaign editor, select ETH and review the budget,
   gifts and existing commitments. The editor checks available funds and offers
   to deposit any remaining shortfall before publication. Depositing alone
   neither reserves a budget nor publishes a campaign.

**New fund** supports other purpose slugs using the same metadata/creation flow.
Verified additions enter the admin chart and public Fund Us chart, splits and
bunny rotation on creation/refresh. **Archive selected allocation** deactivates
it on-chain, stops deposits/payouts (including referral claims), and removes it
from active charts and Fund Us. Nothing is deleted: the admin archive retains
both balances, and **Manage / restore** exposes restoration and owner recovery.
Consider outstanding commitments before archiving or recovering.

Creation, deposits, ETH recovery and archive/restore have explicit review dialogs.

ETH recovery sends only to the registered owner, including while inactive.
Exact router event receipts are verified; uncertain broadcasts remain locked.
Use **Unresolved ETH / archive transaction** and the original/replacement hash
before retrying. An unrelated failed receipt never unlocks the action. These
journals are browser-local, not protection across devices or cleared storage.
Existing USDC receipt controls and journal keys are preserved.

Reuse decision: adapt the existing [public chart renderer](../js/fund-visual.mjs),
[fund discovery and ETH contribution journal](../js/fund-contribution.mjs),
[metadata/creation/USDC helpers](../js/settlement-funds.mjs), and
[referral budget checks](../js/referral-campaign-editor.mjs). The donor contract
is ArtFi's `contracts/ArtFiSettlementRouter.sol` at commit `843e770`:
`allFundIds`, `setFundActive`, `fundNative` and `recoverFund`. It has no deletion;
archival preserves identity/history. No contract or speculative shared package
is added. Shared-router foreign funds are excluded by project metadata identity;
ETH and USDC cannot be interchanged. Receiving-app tests cover creation followed
by exact-wei native funding, lifecycle/owner/role checks, archived recovery and
public-vs-admin discovery. Chrome verification covers review cancellation,
receipt locks, public archive removal and responsive chart views using mocks;
no real transactions or campaign publication are part of validation.

### Referral fund matches

Beneath the Supporter queue, **Referral fund matches owed** handles new
versioned musician campaigns after they end, close or fill. Each approved
newcomer creates only their earned Top10/Playback entries; unfilled slots do
not create debts. The ETH source amount and publication-fixed USDC match are
shown separately, with the newcomer and both BaseScan receipts.

**Release & match** explicitly pays the source share from `dbusk-referrals`
to the configured admin wallet, enabling that router recipient if needed,
then asks for the matching USDC deposit. There is no automatic swap. The
admin must arrange USDC and keep Base ETH for gas. Declining the second step
leaves the verified source paid and the deposit owed; resume with
**Deposit USDC**, without paying the source twice.

Preparations and broadcast hashes are journaled per claim/leg/phase. Unknown,
replaced or timed-out transactions remain protected. **Check receipt** uses
the original or successful matching replacement transaction, not an approval.
**Review unsent** releases only a preparation without a recorded payout or
deposit hash after an explicit wallet-history reason. An unrelated revert
never unlocks a phase. Source release needs an exact canonical, twice-confirmed
`PayrollPaid`; target completion needs exact owner `FundFunded` and native-USDC
transfer proofs. A source reorg blocks the target stage. Source payouts reduce
ETH commitments immediately; only both verified stages mark the fund leg paid.
Pending source payments also block rejection, amendments and archiving.
The queue and Supporter transfers share Payroll's wallet-write lock.

### USDC Deposits

The public fund pills open immediately; wallet names enhance the rows after
transaction proofs appear. The default view shows this week's pending estimates
in full, without a pending-list dropdown. Recent data covers this week plus the
previous two completed New York weeks; the visible activity table stops at the
earliest payment in the second-most-recent weekly payout run, retaining all
payments in that run and newer additions. Earlier activity is available under
**Weekly archives**, which fetches a lightweight week index only when
opened, then each selected week's income, actual payouts and frozen allocation
receipts on demand. Funding-only weeks are included. BaseScan links remain
available for both income and payouts; an allocation is not proof of payment.

The centered **Fund Us** button and About's matching button open the same
contribution modal. Opening About no longer fetches the complete ledger or
resolves its wallets. Fund Us lazily reads the Base router through the shared
public-first read provider. Existing active funds render first; the router's
`allFundIds` registry then supplies additional funds whose public metadata matches
the `decentbusking/settlement-fund/v1` schema, slug/hash, Base chain,
router address and fund ID. Other projects sharing the router are excluded.
Names and descriptions render as text, not markup. Metadata outages or identity
mismatches show an incomplete-discovery warning and retry action without hiding
verified balances. Discovery runs on opening/refreshing, not a background chain
scan; confirming a new fund in this app invalidates the cache and refreshes an
open popup. Results are otherwise shared for 15 seconds and refreshed after
contributions. Failed registry/balance reads disable new contributions and show

an explicit retry state, never invent zero balances.
Custom purpose slugs do not need a `dbusk-` prefix: this preserves the existing
fund creator. The app-specific schema and matching on-chain identity establish
which project's fund it is, not a cosmetic name prefix.

The switchable 3D-style bar/pie visual shows current total balances, not weekly
spendable budgets or fundraising targets. ETH and USDC have separate views and
exact amount labels. Top10 and Playback accept USDC only in this UI; other
active funds offer both USDC and native ETH. ETH is not converted into USDC and
does not increase USDC payroll budgets. The information button explains funding
sources and how to inspect weekly income/payout proofs and router events.
USDC quick fills are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 108 and 1234.

The icon-only bunny walks through every displayed fund, spotlighting its chart
row with purpose and participation guidance. Back/Next/Finish, Escape, keyboard
focus containment and reduced-motion support are included. The guide
owns keyboard input ahead of the page-wide tutorial while its native modal is
on top, so Escape/Tab cannot be intercepted by the older tour. Versioned module
aliases keep cached header/About/tutorial entry points on one contribution UI.
It temporarily shows USDC so every fund is represented, then restores the prior currency. It
does not connect a wallet, fill contribution amounts or request transactions.
Only Playback/Top10 describe weekly artist allocations; work/booking/campaign
funds follow their own approvals, and public pinner rewards remain inactive.
New funds use their metadata `description` and optional text `earningRules`
(up to 2000 characters); missing rules explicitly make no weekly reward promise.

Newly discovered funds enter the chart, selector, splits and guide together.

Each currency has a separate total. Custom splits use either percentages that
total 100% per currency, or exact amounts that sum to that currency's total.
Integer micro-USDC/wei arithmetic preserves every unit; percentage rounding
remainders go to the last selected fund. Review opens a confirmation sidepanel
before any wallet request. It groups USDC into at most one exact remaining-total
approval, then uses one deposit per fund/currency, the minimum supported by the
existing router without a new contract or custody hop. This is not atomic.
Confirmed legs retain their transaction links if a later leg fails or is
cancelled. Contextual receipt/recovery controls live only in that sidepanel.
Continuing checks uncertain receipts and sends only remaining legs. As with single
deposits, this protection is browser-local; clearing storage or changing devices
loses the journal. Never retry an uncertain payment without checking its receipt.
**Stop unsent remainder** abandons only the unsent remainder; it refuses to
unlock an uncertain transaction and never refunds confirmed contributions.

journal, [fund-archive.mjs](../js/fund-archive.mjs), and ArtFi's existing

top-layer spotlight/bunny, keyboard and reduced-motion patterns. Discovery uses

ArtFi's existing `ArtFiSettlementRouter.allFundIds` registry (commit `843e770`),
with Busking-specific metadata checks rather than displaying all shared funds.

Select an existing active fund in Fund Allocations, enter the deposit amount, and confirm the deposit action. The app verifies native Base USDC, six decimals, asset approval, wallet balance, and Base network. It requests an ERC-20 approval only if the current allowance is insufficient, for the exact intended amount rather than an unlimited allowance; then it requests the `fundToken` transaction. Approval is not a deposit. Depositing into a fund is not an artist payout.

Pending approval/deposit stages and hashes are kept in browser storage. An unresolved operation locks another deposit to that fund. Check its receipt or supply the replacement transaction hash; unlocking requires a successful matching Approval/FundFunded event, or the exact recorded reverted transaction. An approval cannot unlock an operation already marked as a deposit. Unknown broadcasts remain locked for wallet-history review.
