# Public radio: audience scale and operating guide

## What changes, in plain language

LiveKit is the interactive studio: the performer, producer and independent audio
receiver need real-time connections. Putting every audience member in that studio
uses a participant seat for each connection. A monthly allowance of participant
minutes does not raise the simultaneous-seat limit.

HLS is the public radio distribution line. The server produces one continuous
audio programme, cuts it into four-second files and uploads it to Cloudflare.
Listeners obtain those files from its CDN, not individual LiveKit seats. Programme
updates also use the CDN; moving audio alone would leave hundreds of browsers
polling Render directly.

This trades immediate sound for approximately 10-20 seconds of delay. It is not
unlimited capacity, and it does not make the studio or Render server unnecessary.
The same programme includes rotation, paid adverts and successive performers.
Scheduled studio changes must not cut off the previous act's buffered ending.

The new path defaults **off**. Deploying an empty CDN Worker does not select it
for production listeners. Begin with approved show/rehearsal windows, not 24/7
encoding.

The public HLS feed remains the main-radio audio clock. When a queued MP4
reaches that clock, the browser shows its muted video through the existing
radio media endpoint. An audio-only entry, a live set, or leaving radio
clears the picture. If the picture fails, audio continues with a visible
notice. These on-demand video requests use the radio media proxy, not the
audio CDN, and are not covered by the audio-only capacity measurements below.

## The separate limits

| Limit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| LiveKit simultaneous participants | Studio/direct-listener seats, shared across the project. Its documented Build limit is 100; the existing temporary direct-listener cap reserves headroom. Verify the actual account before each rehearsal. |
| Monthly allowances | Minutes, transfer, requests and operations included in each provider's plan. These are not simultaneous-audience guarantees. |
| Render CPU and memory | The bot, receiver, encoder and existing radio work share a machine. The currently inspected instance has 0.5 CPU and 512 MB; no upgrade follows from this feature. |
| Audio transfer | At 128 kbps, one listener uses roughly 57.6 MB/hour; 200 use roughly 11.52 GB/hour, before transport overhead. This is arithmetic, not a measured bill or capacity result. |
| CDN requests | Playlist refreshes, audio files and programme snapshots all count. Cached Worker requests still count. A shared-NAT audience needs a sufficient per-IP request allowance. |

Workers Paid has a $5/month minimum, with usage allowances and metered overages.
R2 Standard has included storage/operation allowances and no Internet-egress fee,
but remains a metered, auto-renewing subscription. Neither estimate is a hard
spending cap. Always-on publishing consumes operations even without listeners.
At 200 listeners, approximate two-second playlist/state polling plus one audio
file every four seconds is about 900,000 Worker requests per show hour, before
startup and retries. The current Paid allowance of 10 million requests per
month would cover roughly eleven such hours if nothing else used it; CPU,
storage and R2 operations have separate allowances. A CDN cache hit avoids

re-reading an object but is still a Worker request. This is a planning estimate,
not a per-show fixed price, measured invoice or budget ceiling.
Consult current [Workers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/),
[R2 pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/) and
[Render bandwidth](https://render.com/docs/outbound-bandwidth).

## Source, privacy and performer attribution

- Rotation/adverts use JukeLoop's actually consumed Opus packets, not its prefetch.
- Live audio reuses the independent receiver only for the exact authorized,
  armed, fresh public booking. Private practice, backstage, suspended/filler
  periods and unrelated rooms cannot feed this path.
- Broadcasting permission is independent of permission to make an archive.
  HLS does not turn on recording or create an IPFS archive.
- R2 stays private. Only the authenticated Worker accepts backend uploads.
  Public objects expire within 120 seconds even after an encoder crash; cache
  lifetimes cannot extend their expiry. A cleanup cron removes expired objects.
  Upload expiry allows up to 30 seconds of publisher-ahead clock skew, but the
  edge clamps stored expiry to 120 seconds from receipt. Expired, malformed or
  further-ahead deadlines still fail with HTTP 400 and `INVALID_UPLOAD_EXPIRY`.
  This avoids rejecting fast playlist uploads at the exact two-minute boundary.
- The player labels the programme from actual media programme time. Tips bind to
  that audible booking and its exact performer, not the next studio performer.
  Reactions pause when the delayed audible act differs from the current studio act.
- Publisher self-return protection, archive listening and Ads Only remain
  separate. Errors never silently consume a LiveKit listener seat.

## Configure and deploy in order

1. Obtain explicit billing approval; activate Workers Paid and R2 through normal
   Cloudflare access. Create the private Standard bucket named in
   [wrangler.toml](../cloudflare/wrangler.toml). Do not enable public R2 access.
2. Validate and deploy the independent edge:

   ```sh
   npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --config cloudflare/wrangler.toml
   npx wrangler deploy --config cloudflare/wrangler.toml
   npx wrangler secret put BROADCAST_UPLOAD_TOKEN --config cloudflare/wrangler.toml
   ```

   Generate a separate 32-200 character URL-safe upload secret. Use the private
   secret prompt/input, never a command-line literal, source file or screenshot.
   The Worker requires both its R2 binding and rate limiter. The latter allows
   24,000 requests/minute per IP/location: 200 shared-NAT clients can exceed
   15,000/minute with bootstrap, state, playlist and segment requests.
   This approximate per-location limit is not a global spending cap.
3. Configure the publisher's server-only environment:

   - `PUBLIC_BROADCAST_MODE=preview`: encode/upload, but keep the ordinary public
     radio transport. `direct` is the default and does not run the encoder.
   - `PUBLIC_BROADCAST_EDGE_URL`: exact HTTPS Worker origin, no path or credentials.
   - `PUBLIC_BROADCAST_UPLOAD_TOKEN`: the same dedicated private upload secret.
   - `FFMPEG_PATH`: optional override of the existing FFmpeg executable.

   Native 48 kHz stereo AAC encoding must work on the deployment architecture.
   A local ignored environment file is not a Render environment update.
4. Prewarm the preview for at least 20 seconds. Verify continuous segment,
   playlist and state publication, real AAC playback and Linux container metrics.

Do not start a second production Discord bot from a worktree.
5. Run the agreed staged workload and an actual browser/hardware rehearsal.
   Selecting `public` for production requires separate operator approval after
   reviewing the evidence. Deploy readers before selecting that mode.

Do not bypass the existing radio predeploy guard. The public protected tail
adds 40 seconds of deployment protection after paid/ad/live packets. A change
of transport or service restart can still interrupt listening; schedule the
switch outside a protected show. To roll back, have the producer explicitly
select `direct` only with the bounded direct-seat allowance verified, or stop
the public broadcast. There is no automatic mass fallback.

Quiet DJuke playlist event scans retain a durable cursor after at least one
complete scan chunk of progress. Short empty polls still avoid uploads, but a
replacement worker no longer needs to replay an indefinitely old quiet range.
This uses the existing required-mirror checkpoint path; failed cursor writes
remain errors and do not advance the durable boundary. The first catch-up from
an older checkpoint must still complete before the safe deployment gate opens.
The deployed cursor repair was read back successfully near the current chain
head through the existing checkpoint store, with the six batch records retained.

The encoder, Opus decoding, HLS pacing and uploads run in a dedicated Node
worker thread in the same container, not another service. This keeps unrelated
bot event-loop stalls out of the audio clock. The parent forwards only the
selected public source, with bounded in-flight messages; source age across the
thread boundary is not used to cut an active song, and the PCM queue is bounded

at sixty seconds of audio for the same stalled-main-loop protection. By the
owner's boundary-sync decision, songs are not cut when a bot stall leaves late
PCM, including their final queued samples after the producer begins the gong.
Only queued `gap:` padding may be retired when the next radio programme arrives;
song, paid and live PCM remain ordered and intact. Recovery reports
`PCM_GAP_CATCHUP` with the amount of padding removed.
The browser stays at normal playback speed, disables Hls.js's maximum-latency
auto-seek, and seeks only within a known audible gap. Its target is capped
250 ms before the next programme, with a 250 ms onset margin; without a known
gap end it waits rather than skipping into music. Excess delay may require more
than one gong to recover. An unavailable/expired stream is still an explicit
failure, not a guarantee of uninterrupted playback through an outage.
Malformed PCM still fails closed.
The encoder's scheduling-stall limit, private-room gates and protected tail remain.
In-flight credits are decremented by the worker through a shared atomic counter,
not by parent-loop acknowledgment callbacks. Otherwise a busy parent can falsely
count already processed frames as backlogged. Limit failures include a bounded
stage/count diagnostic, distinguishing IPC backlog, PCM size and source age.
Public state is requested from the parent through the existing eight-second
deadline, and worker errors explicitly make the broadcast unavailable.
Object PUTs may retry fast network/408/500/502/503/504 failures at most three
times with bounded backoff, sharing the original eight-second deadline rather
than restarting it. Identical object keys/bytes make these retries idempotent.
Authorization, other client errors and exhausted budgets still fail explicitly.

Publication errors expose only a bounded stage and HTTP status/timeout name,
distinguishing state reads, object uploads and local staging without disclosing
credentials or filesystem errors. Audio age/queue/clock limits do not change.

Preview mode samples the parent CPU only when explicitly enabled with
`PUBLIC_BROADCAST_PROFILE_CPU=true`, at 10 ms for at most ten resource windows.
Leave it unset for normal, production-equivalent preview measurements. Only
windows with an event-loop maximum above 500 ms log
`[radio-cpu-stall]`: a top-ten aggregate of module-relative file, function, line
and sampled time, never a raw profile, payload, credential or absolute path.
Direct/public modes do not start this diagnostic. Health reports the measured
event-loop maximum alongside p99, since a rare multi-second pause can be hidden
by an otherwise healthy percentile. Sampling is diagnostic overhead, not proof
that a particular function caused a pause.
Container memory also exposes anonymous, file and inactive-file counters from
`memory.stat` when available. Under the owner's 18 Nov rule below, the scored
percentage is the working set, `(memory.current - inactive_file) / memory.max`,
which matches Render's memory graph; raw `memory.current / memory.max` is still
reported. Missing optional breakdown falls back to the raw value; it does not
erase otherwise valid quota samples or turn them into passes.

The client uses native HLS only with a usable programme clock (`getStartDate`),
otherwise the self-hosted pinned Hls.js bundle. Native playback capability
alone is insufficient to identify the audible performer. The Hls.js initial
sync target is three segments; playback stays at normal speed rather than
fast-forwarding a buffered song ending. A listener more than six segments

(about 24 s) behind the playlist edge, roughly 26-30 s by the clock, jumps back
to the sync target instead of drifting further. Before 18 Nov the limit was
unbounded, so every stall added permanent delay (owner choice: jump, not speed
up). AAC decoding is required. An embedded
browser without AAC is not evidence that Safari or full Chrome decoded the
broadcast.

## Frozen acceptance limits and evidence

Before the scored staging rehearsal, the operator approved:

- 200 public listeners for 10 minutes.
- Metadata request p95 at most 1.5 seconds; decoded audio-start p95 at most
  3 seconds. Download latency is **not** audio-start latency.
- Zero server 5xx responses.
- Container CPU at most 70% of its actual quota; memory at most 75%.
  On the inspected 0.5-CPU/512-MB plan, these correspond to 0.35 CPU and 384 MB.
- Event-loop p99 below 200 ms. Separately measure audible delay against the
  10-20 second HLS target and inspect silence, overlap, reconnects and boundaries.

On 18 Nov 2026 the owner amended two limits: memory is the working set
(excluding reclaimable inactive file cache) at most 85% of the container
limit, about 435 MiB of 512 MiB, and audible delay p95 at most 30 seconds.
The other limits above are unchanged, and the public mode stays unselected
until the owner confirms it.

`/health.radioResources` reports Node CPU/RSS/heap/event-loop values and Linux
cgroup v2 container CPU/memory where available. Only container values include
FFmpeg and the other container processes. Verify their reported quotas match
the hosting plan. Missing counters or missing samples are **unmeasured**, not a
headroom pass.

For development only, start the isolated synthetic fixture:

```sh
node test/helpers/broadcast-preview.cjs
node scripts/broadcast-load.mjs --origin http://127.0.0.1:8331 --listeners 200 --seconds 60
```

It does not connect to Discord, LiveKit, a wallet or production state. Supplying
the server-only edge environment explicitly sends synthetic audio to the approved
test edge instead of the in-memory local edge. Stop it after the check.
For authorized non-production hosting, the workload runner requires

`--staging-approved` and a matching explicit `--media-origin` when different.
It rejects the known production hostname and never signs, votes or settles fees.
Its result remains HTTP-only and unscored; no aggregate test count certifies
200-listener capacity or a successful human rehearsal.

Development evidence so far:

audience capacity, and further live observation must not be reported as already
performed.

## Reuse decision

Need: distribute the complete public programme without per-listener LiveKit
seats, while preserving public/private gates and exact performer attribution.
The searched scope was Canopy's relevant curated offers and current Busking
source, tests, issues/PRs and worktrees; it was not a whole-library inventory.
Adapt Busking at `35f9a96d34c552a98cbc14a7b5c6acb9dd01b41f`:
`createLiveAudioService`'s independently verified PCM,
JukeLoop's `_startPrepared` consumed-resource path, and the existing shared
radio audio element and deployment guard. No compatible whole-program HLS
donor was identified in that inspected scope. The small publisher, edge and
HLS player are new; no speculative shared framework is extracted.
Existing Apache-2.0 Busking code and third-party notices remain applicable.
For compact checkpoint identities, reuse Busking's existing
`discord-bot/checkpoint-history.js:contentHash` from `973f806`; no new hash
dependency or shared abstraction is needed. The receiving checkpoint,
retention and required-mirror tests pass, including the measured retained-heap
regression; hosted validation remains a separate gate.
The website-only advert clock adapts the existing `devert-loop.js`
controller and its injected `createStream` seam; FFmpeg's own header read
supplies the length because the deployed bundle has no `ffprobe`.
Edge publish recovery adapts the `stateIssue` deferral from `02d5987` (#400)
and reuses the uploader's existing transient-error classification.
Receiving tests include actual FFmpeg AAC decode across advert/A/B/advert,
wrong/private-room exclusion, delayed tip binding, zero-seat HLS admission,
state coalescing/expiry, quota normalization and legacy-radio regressions.

Hosted capacity, a genuine multi-human rehearsal and hardware Safari remain
separate evidence gates until actually performed.

Inter-Song Gong / Bell / Chime

Five 6-second padded boundaries. Each starts quietly and fades out gently.

🏆 The community makes the chart

👍 Every vote moves the music

Songs rank by this week’s net votes: upvotes minus downvotes. Use the radio’s thumbs while a song plays. The chart updates live; each song holds its own place, even when one artist has several hits.

💸 A weekly prize ladder

First place receives half the available weekly Top 10 pot. Each next place receives half the remainder, and the final payable place gets the rest. Every payable prize must exceed $0.10 USDC; a smaller pot supports fewer prizes.

Shown prizes are estimates, not guaranteed payments. Rankings and estimates freeze at Monday midnight in America/New_York. Artist payout wallets must be linked, and payments require owner approval.

Use the same artist wallet on your mint request. A radio play counts after at least 30 seconds of completed, audible Discord playback. Votes help guide the rotation; they do not add paid plays.

When a weekly budget is funded, the owner reviews and settles eligible payouts in USDC on Base. A tally is not a promise of payment: no funded budget means no playback payout. Check My Playback Tally for recorded plays and the Payroll panel for the current weekly draft.

🛠️ Build and earn

Pick an open GitHub issue, ask to be assigned, and submit a pull request that says Closes #issue-number. Only work with a bounty label, such as bounty: 10 USDC or bounty: 10 ART, enters the repo payout queue after the pull request merges.

The owner reviews and settles eligible rewards from the funded Base treasury. No bounty label means no automatic repo payout; never add or guess a bounty amount yourself.

🎨 Help without coding

Make or share art: offer original, shareable cover art, posters, or video assets. Artists can add optional cover art to a mint request. For project-wide art, open an issue first and tell us how we may use it.

Help with the gallery: suggest an artist spotlight, a themed listening playlist, or a better way to show community artwork in the archive. The gallery is an idea to help shape, not a separate paid feature today.

Test and welcome people: listen, vote, try the site on your phone, report a clear bug, invite an artist, or host a listening session. These are welcome contributions, but are not automatically paid.

Want payment for a specific art, testing, or outreach task? Ask the maintainer to agree on the task and bounty before starting. It must be tracked through an eligible GitHub issue and accepted submission; repo payroll does not pay for informal activity.

🎟️ DecentBusking Supporter DNFTs

Supporter DNFTs are a separate thank-you from music NFTs. The v1.0.0 edition is listed on Base for $100 USDC. Review the live listing and stock below; each purchase requires an exact USDC approval and a separate wallet confirmation.

# Earn by pinning: keep the music, share the rewards

[Wiki home](Home.md) · [Technical design](../docs/PINNER-NETWORK.md) · [Open DecentBusking](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/)

Every song on DecentBusking lives on IPFS: a public, content-addressed network
where anyone can keep an exact copy of a file. Today most of our copies sit with
one hosting company (Pinata) and one operator computer. **Each new pinner is
another independent home for the music.** If one copy goes dark, the radio
keeps playing from the others. The more pinners we have, the more *decent*
(decentralized) we become.

In return, approved pinners share a weekly fund in Base USDC.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["💻 Run IPFS Desktop"] --> B["📌 Pin the shared music"]
  B --> C["✍️ Join and sign"]
  C --> D["✅ Admin approves"]
  D --> E["🔍 Surprise checks, about hourly"]
  E --> F["💸 Weekly USDC share"]
```

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **What you keep** | About **2.2 GB** today (November 2026): every song in the radio and jukebox catalogue (279), 17 Jones Drive Sessions albums and the public playlist record. It grows as musicians add songs. |
| **What you need** | A computer that stays on most of the day, at least 10 GB free disk space, home internet, and a Base wallet linked to your Discord account in **Profile**. |
| **What you earn** | A share of the weekly `dbusk-pinners` fund. It receives 8% of every song payment and a quarter of each radio fee. Each week, 100% of the fund's unreserved closing balance is split between qualifying pinners, weighted by passed checks. |
| **Who can join** | Musicians and listeners. One Discord member = one wallet = one node. An admin approves every node. |
| **What it costs** | No fees and no gas. Joining is a free signature. You supply electricity, disk space and bandwidth. |

A Pinata account or a single click on **Pin** doesn't earn rewards on its own.
Rewards come from your own node answering our independent checks.

## Choose your path

| Path | Best for | Rewards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Your everyday computer** | Most people. IPFS Desktop on Mac, Windows or Linux. | Yes |
| **2. An always-on box** | An old laptop, mini PC, Raspberry Pi 4/5 with an SSD, or a home server. The best uptime. | Yes |
| **3. Help without rewards** | Pin a copy to your own Pinata account from the IPFS button. It's a welcome backup, but we can't independently check that it's yours. | No |
## Path 1: step by step

### 1. Install IPFS Desktop

Download it from [docs.ipfs.tech](https://docs.ipfs.tech/install/ipfs-desktop/)
and open it. In its settings, turn on **Launch at login**. If your computer's
firewall asks whether IPFS may accept incoming connections, choose **Allow**.

Turn off automatic sleep while plugged in, or your node can't answer checks:

- **Mac:** System Settings → Energy (or Battery → Options) → *Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off*.
- **Windows:** Settings → System → Power → Sleep: *Never* when plugged in.

### 2. Let DecentBusking talk to your node

Your browser needs permission to read your node's ID and to pin your private
ownership marker. In IPFS Desktop open **Settings → IPFS Config**, find the
`"API"` section and make it look like this. Keep any other entries you
already have.

```json
"API": {
  "HTTPHeaders": {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": ["https://thejollylama.github.io", "http://127.0.0.1:5001", "https://webui.ipfs.io"],
    "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": ["PUT", "POST", "GET"]
  }
},
```

Save, then restart IPFS from the IPFS Desktop menu. If your browser asks
whether the site may reach devices on your local network, allow it.

> Never add `"*"`, and never open port 5001 to the internet. Port 5001 controls
> your node; only this computer should reach it.

### 3. Check that the internet can reach you

Our checker connects straight to your node from the internet. Most home
routers open the way automatically (UPnP). Give a freshly started node about
10 minutes, then run:

- **Mac/Linux (Terminal):** `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5001/api/v0/swarm/addrs/autonat`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5001/api/v0/swarm/addrs/autonat`

`"reachability":"Public"` means you're ready. If it says `Private` or `Unknown`:

- In your router's admin page, turn on **UPnP**, or forward port **4001**
  (TCP and UDP) to this computer.
- Mobile hotspots and some internet providers (carrier-grade NAT) can't accept
  incoming connections at all. Use [Path 2](#path-2-an-always-on-box) on a
  rented server instead.

### 4. Pin the shared music

Pick one:

- **Easy:** open [DecentBusking](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/),
  press the **IPFS** button on the left of the header, choose **IPFS Desktop**
  and press **Pin shared data**. Keep the tab open. The first run downloads
  about 2.2 GB and can take an hour or more; later runs only fetch what's new.
  Press it again about **once a week** to pick up new songs.
- **Hands-free (recommended):** run the [sync helper](#the-sync-helper). It
  does the same job every 15 minutes with no browser tab.

Pinning never deletes anything. You can stop and resume at any time.

### 5. Join and get approved

1. Connect your Base wallet in the header and link Discord in **Profile**.
2. Open the **IPFS** button → **Join pinner rewards** and sign. It's free, with
   no gas. Your node pins a small, random *ownership marker* that never leaves
   your computer.
3. Tell an admin in the DecentBusking Discord that you've joined. When they
   press **Verify node & approve**, our checker connects directly to your node
   and must find your marker. If approval fails, revisit step 3.

### 6. Stay on and earn

- About once an hour, at unpredictable times, a fresh checker connects only to
  your node. It asks for your marker and random pieces of a random item from
  the shared list. Only your own node can pass. Public gateways and Pinata
  copies don't count.
- The week closes **Monday 00:00 New York time**. To qualify, you need at
  least **20 checks**, at least **90% passed**, and one passed check in the
  final 24 hours.
- **Your share** = your passed checks ÷ everyone's passed checks × the week's
  unreserved pinner fund. Watch your running estimate in the IPFS panel.
  Estimates can change until the week closes.
- After the close, an admin pays the frozen weekly receipt in Base USDC with an
  owner-signed payroll transaction. The panel shows **awaiting payroll** and
  then **paid on Base**.

Twenty checks take about a day of uptime, so join by about Saturday to have a
chance at that week's close.

## The sync helper

The helper keeps your node in step with the shared list. Every 15 minutes it
pins anything new and never removes anything. It needs:

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22 or newer.
- A copy of this repository (18 MB). Use `git clone`, or **Code → Download ZIP** on GitHub.

No `npm install`, keys, wallet or secrets are needed.

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking.git
cd DecentBusking
node discord-bot/community-pinner-client.js --watch
```

Brand-new songs may not be announced on the IPFS network yet. For those, the
helper downloads a *verified copy* (a CAR file) from Pinata's public gateway.
IPFS checks every block against its content ID, so a gateway can't slip in
different bytes. Set `PINNER_CAR_GATEWAY` to use another trustless gateway.
Each pinner who holds a song also makes it easier for the next pinner to fetch.

Update occasionally with `git pull`, then restart the helper.

### Start the helper automatically

Replace `/Users/YOU/DecentBusking` with your copy's folder, and the node path
with the output of `which node` (Mac/Linux) or `where node` (Windows).

#### Mac (launchd)

Save as `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.decentbusking.community-pinner.plist`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>com.decentbusking.community-pinner</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key><array>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin/node</string>
    <string>/Users/YOU/DecentBusking/discord-bot/community-pinner-client.js</string>
    <string>--watch</string>
  </array>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>
  <key>KeepAlive</key><true/>
  <key>ThrottleInterval</key><integer>30</integer>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/Library/Logs/community-pinner.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/Library/Logs/community-pinner.err.log</string>
</dict></plist>
```

```sh
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.decentbusking.community-pinner.plist
tail -f ~/Library/Logs/community-pinner.log
```

#### Linux (systemd user service)

Save as `~/.config/systemd/user/community-pinner.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=DecentBusking community pinner
After=network-online.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /home/YOU/DecentBusking/discord-bot/community-pinner-client.js --watch
Restart=always
RestartSec=30

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

```sh
systemctl --user enable --now community-pinner
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"   # keep running after you log out
journalctl --user -u community-pinner -f
```

#### Windows (Task Scheduler)

```powershell
schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /TN "DecentBusking pinner" /TR "\"C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe\" C:\Users\YOU\DecentBusking\discord-bot\community-pinner-client.js --watch"
```

## Path 2: an always-on box

1. Install [Kubo](https://docs.ipfs.tech/install/command-line/) (the IPFS
   command-line node), run `ipfs init`, and start `ipfs daemon` as a service.
   On a Raspberry Pi, keep the IPFS data on an SSD, not the SD card.
2. Allow the site, then restart the daemon:

   ```sh
   ipfs config --json API.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Origin '["https://thejollylama.github.io"]'
   ipfs config --json API.HTTPHeaders.Access-Control-Allow-Methods '["PUT","POST","GET"]'
   ```

3. Check reachability with `ipfs swarm addrs autonat`, as in step 3.
4. Run the [sync helper](#the-sync-helper) on the box.
5. Joining happens in your browser, which must reach the box's port 5001
   privately. Open an SSH tunnel from your laptop, then join while it's open:

   ```sh
   ssh -N -L 5001:127.0.0.1:5001 you@your-box
   ```

## Disk space

- The shared list is about 2.2 GB and grows with each new song (a few MB each)
  and album. Keep at least 10 GB free.
- IPFS Desktop's automatic cleanup removes only *unpinned* cache. Your pinned
  music is never cleaned up.
- If your node also holds other content, raise its storage limit in IPFS Config
  (`Datastore.StorageMax`, default 10 GB).

## Privacy and safety

- You only hold content that is already public: songs, albums and the public
  playlist record. That record includes song credits, uploaders' Discord names
  and IDs, tip wallets, and play and vote tallies. It contains no private keys,
  passwords or message text.
- Like any peer-to-peer app, your node's internet (IP) address is visible to
  other IPFS peers. DecentBusking doesn't publish it. Public receipts show only
  your wallet, node ID, check counts and amounts. If that's a concern, use a
  rented server (Path 2).
- Never share your Pinata key or wallet recovery phrase, and never expose port 5001.
- The ownership marker is random bytes that stay on your node. It proves the node is yours.

## Troubleshooting

| You see | Try |
| --- | --- |
| *Detecting your IPFS Desktop peer…* fails, or *Failed to fetch* | Redo [step 2](#2-let-decentbusking-talk-to-your-node), restart IPFS and allow local-network access in the browser. |
| Approval says your node can't be reached | Redo [step 3](#3-check-that-the-internet-can-reach-you) until it says `Public`. |
| *verified gateway copy failed: gateway returned 403* | That item isn't publicly downloadable yet. A few missing items won't stop you qualifying. |
| *Not yet qualified* | You need 20 checks. Keep the computer awake and IPFS running. |
| You reinstalled IPFS or lost the marker | IPFS panel → **Reset lost node marker**, then ask for approval again. Earlier awards are kept. |
| You want to switch wallets | Ask an admin to suspend the old node first. Awards already frozen stay with the old wallet. |
